correctness.rationale: The classical three-move chain EF strategy matches all nonempty chains of sizes at least seven, and coordinatewise composition of EF strategies preserves all atomic order/equality relations on product pairs. Hence all parameters reduce to the 28 rectangles with sorted side lengths at most seven. The exact recursive Hintikka types T0,T1,T2,T3 are equivalent by backward induction to a three-move EF game, including repeating points and moves from either structure. Two independent source implementations evaluated all 28 finite cases, producing an identical 21-class canonical map and proving the largest minimum representative has 30 elements. This is a logically valid exhaustive finite proof after an infinite reduction, not an extrapolation.

value.rationale: The two-chain product is a canonical family of finite distributive lattices and bounded-rank order theories are natural invariants. The complete classification identifies exactly which size pairs cannot be distinguished by three quantifiers in the weak pure-order language. The sharp representative bound 30 substantially improves the immediate product-preservation bound 49 and demonstrates nontrivial cross-factor mergers while retaining 21 distinct theories. No downstream theorem is claimed or required.
